session.title: The Tower in the Stone
session.inWorldStart: Late afternoon, Day 5 of mountain ascent (~2 days after Session 18)
session.openingContext: Party is mid-travel at higher elevation. Adrik is now with them. The session opens with a brief narrative bridge compressing 2 days of climbing, then begins proper at the bat ambush at a switchback.

hiddenConditions.subject: Tyr
hiddenConditions.note: Carrying over from S18. Long rests can decrement.

hiddenConditions.subject: Tyr
hiddenConditions.note: DC 12 INT save before each long rest, or +1 exhaustion. Tracking continues.

hiddenConditions.subject: Adrik
hiddenConditions.note: Carries the locator pendant. The pendant ONLY reacts within ½ mile of a shard. Stays cold for early session. Will activate once party closes on Amon Lhuin (Scene 5B trail or Scene 6 approach).

tickingClocks.label: The pit prisoners
tickingClocks.detail: 9 swamp village survivors are in the lower workings. Each long rest the party takes BEFORE reaching the lair, 1 prisoner risks death (DM call — narrative). If 4+ days pass before rescue, the party finds bodies, not survivors.

tickingClocks.label: Pharazôr's awareness
tickingClocks.detail: He has been watching the bat couriers' reports. Knows a small armed group climbed past the bear cove. Does NOT yet know about Adrik or Tyr's sword specifically. Will learn both during Scene 8.

tickingClocks.label: The shard
tickingClocks.detail: Embedded in the lower workings in a place Pharazôr believes is secured. He is wrong about how secure it is. Adrik's pendant will lead the party to it if Adrik follows the signal.

foreshadowingChecklist.label: Pacts are plural
foreshadowingChecklist.detail: Pharazôr should reference 'agreements like Maldwin's' or 'the others who serve' — implying Maldwin's pact was one of several. Don't name a specific second pact. Just imply the pattern.

foreshadowingChecklist.label: The shard is not unique
foreshadowingChecklist.detail: Without naming what shards ARE, Pharazôr should react to the pendant in a way that says he KNOWS what Adrik is hunting. ('I sense you carry something that should not have come this far north.') Christian decides whether Adrik responds.

foreshadowingChecklist.label: Tyr's smithing house
foreshadowingChecklist.detail: Pharazôr recognizes the Iron of Death's lineage. Names the smith-house (DM call: invent a Númenórean house name on the fly). Line lands as: 'I knew that steel when it was newly forged. Your great-grandfather's grandfather, perhaps.' Tyr-mirror beat.

foreshadowingChecklist.label: Dwarven workings have a name
foreshadowingChecklist.detail: Adrik can read a name carved on the lintel on a Nat 20 History. DM: don't invent it; Christian gets first refusal to name it. Otherwise leave it unread.

foreshadowingChecklist.label: Gothmog NOT named this session
foreshadowingChecklist.detail: Pharazôr alludes to 'my master' or 'the hand that holds the chain' once at most. No further specificity.

mustBeTrue: The party has fought bats in force.
The party has reached Amon Lhuin (whether by abduction or tracking).

Pharazôr has been seen and named on screen, OR (if combat ended the session before audience) the party has direct evidence of his existence (his throne room, his journal, his spoken voice from another room).
Adrik's pendant has reacted visibly enough that the rest of the party noticed at least once.
canHappen: The shard is recovered by Adrik (or anyone).
A direct fight with Pharazôr begins (vs. ending the session before combat).

npcs.name: Giant Bat Courier × 4–6
npcs.surfaceRead: Leather-winged, eerily coordinated, the size of large dogs in flight
npcs.hidden: Pharazôr's aerial network. Trained to subdue and carry, not to kill outright. Will retreat if reduced below half number.
npcs.stats: Use a giant bat statblock (AME or 5e). HP ~22, AC 13, fly 60 ft. Bite +4 for 1d6+2.

npcs.name: Bat Alpha × 1
npcs.surfaceRead: Larger than the others; an iron harness fitted across its chest
npcs.hidden: The carrier. Targets the smallest/lightest exposed PC (Dudo, Mungo, or Adrik are 3'–4'6"). Harness can sustain a halfling-weight payload mid-flight.
npcs.stats: HP ~38, AC 13, fly 60 ft (50 ft when burdened). Bite +5 for 1d8+3. Grapple opposed STR. While grappling: AC -2, can fly carrying ~150 lb.

npcs.name: Orc Lair Guards × 3
npcs.surfaceRead: Heavy boots, ill-fitting Númenórean-cut armor, hostile but disciplined
npcs.hidden: Sleep in shifts in the watchtower's outer chamber. Will challenge intruders. Can be bypassed by stealth (DC 14). Their boot prints match the trail Gilgamesh found in S18.
npcs.stats: HP ~30 each, AC 14 (chain shirt), Scimitar +5 for 1d6+3. Javelin +5 for 1d6+3 (range 30/120).

npcs.name: The Pit Prisoners (9 swamp villagers, including Mez)
npcs.surfaceRead: Bruised, malnourished, frightened. MEZ is among them — the innkeeper from the swamp village (S13), gaunt and silent.
npcs.hidden: After party left swamp village in S17.2, Pharazôr's bat swarms harvested survivors. The 9 in pit are what's left of ~48 villagers (rest dead). Mez survived ~3 weeks because he's useful (cooking for prisoners). His 'you left us' beat should land flat — not blame, grief.
npcs.stats: Non-combatants. HP 1d4 each effectively. Cannot fight; can move slowly.

npcs.name: Pharazôr the Architect
npcs.surfaceRead: Tall, ash-pale, dark-eyed, clearly old in a way that's not normal — a Man who has lived too long. Wears Númenórean-cut robes long out of fashion. Speaks formally, in the cadence of someone who has had centuries to choose his words.
npcs.hidden: Black Númenórean. Architect of pacts like Maldwin's. Reports to Gothmog but operates with broad freedom. Has a private agenda: collecting shards. Will sense Adrik's pendant as wrongness without identifying it. Recognizes Iron of Death's smithing-house lineage. WILL OFFER TERMS before fighting. Roughly 800 years old.
npcs.stats: DM judgment — he's a major NPC. Suggested: HP 95, AC 16, Cha-based caster + martial. Has a Númenórean longsword. Avoid running him as a stat block until necessary; he's a story figure first.

scenes.title: The Climb
scenes.subtitle: Narrative bridge — 3 days compressed
scenes.trigger: Opens the session. Cold open, no recap.
scenes.location: The High Pass — three days deeper than where Session 18 left off.
scenes.lighting: Midday on Day 5 of mountain ascent (third day of climbing since S18 ended). Pale sun, thin cold wind, breath visible.
scenes.readAloud:
Three days have passed since the bears.

The mountains do not give them up easily. The trail steepens until walking becomes work and breathing becomes work and rest stops come oftener than any of you would prefer. Five miles a day, on the good days. Less on the bad. The air thins as you climb, and you find yourselves stopping to catch breath at moments that should not have been hard — pulling yourselves up over a ledge, shouldering a pack, calling back to the line. None of you say it, but all of you feel it: the lowlands are below you, and your bodies are not made for this height.

The cold settles in. Nights at this elevation are sharp and starlit and unforgiving. The bear meat from the cove lasts the first day and a half. The lembas is rationed after that. Carl insists he isn't hungry. He is.

Adrik travels with you. The first day he barely speaks — keeps to the back of the line, watches the trail behind. By the evening of the second day, he and Borin are walking close enough to share words; on the third morning, Adrik shares the last of his pipe-weed with him, and neither of them comments on it. Carl reaches a hand back at one point on a bad patch of scree, and Adrik takes it without hesitation. By the third dusk, the silences in camp feel less like distance and more like the kind of quiet that grows between people who have been cold and tired together. Adrik knows what he carries. The party doesn't, and hasn't asked.

Each of the three nights, Borin sets his hand to the stone of the mountain and asks it the question he has asked a hundred times. The first night: no. The second night: no. On the third night, his hand rests against the rock a long moment before he opens his eyes. Yes. Within three miles. He cannot say how many. He cannot say where. Just: yes.

Twice, around a bend on the trail, you have seen a single bat — alone, large, unhurried — wheel against the late afternoon sky and disappear north over the ridges. Nobody has mentioned it. Everyone saw it.

Now it is midday on the fourth day out from the cove. The trail folds and switches across a high traverse where the air thins further. Behind you, the lowlands have flattened into a green-grey haze. Ahead, the High Pass climbs toward a notch between two peaks still streaked with last winter's snow. You have a few hours of full daylight before the sun begins its drop behind the western ridge.

What do you do?
scenes.purpose: 1) Compress 3 days into one immersive monologue. 2) Establish altitude/hunger/cold pressure. 3) Build Adrik bonding through concrete shared moments. 4) Plant the bat — twice seen, going north, unspoken. 5) Plant Borin's 'yes' — orcs within 3 miles, no specifics. 6) Drop the party at midday with daylight to spare for the hunt decision.
dmNotes: ADRIK'S PENDANT IS COLD. The pendant only reacts within ½ mile of a shard, and the party isn't yet within range of Amon Lhuin. Do NOT pass any private information to Christian during this scene. The pendant will activate later (Scene 5B trail or Scene 6 approach).

BORIN'S RUMOR OF THE EARTH gives only YES/NO — no direction, no count. Played as: Day 1 night NO, Day 2 night NO, Day 3 night YES (within 3 miles). 'Yes' is genuinely ambiguous. Could be the orc lair guards, could be orc scouts on the next ridge, could be both. Don't commit to specifics.
OPENING STYLE: Pure cold open. Read the monologue. Do not recap S18. Adrik bonded with the party through the climb (concrete moments + atmospheric quiet) — this is now the established baseline.

skillChecks.context: Anyone observing the surroundings — the mountain feels wrong.

tiers.outcome: Nothing unusual stands out. The mountain is just the mountain.
The larger game has been driven from this part of the range. Something feels off.
All the above. Plus: birds of prey are scarce. The wrongness has a shape — predators are AVOIDING this area.
All the above. Plus: the hunter notices old droppings and fresh — but no mid-aged sign. Animals stopped passing through here suddenly, perhaps a few weeks ago.

All the above. Plus: the hunter spots a single feather-like membrane caught in scrub — large, leathery, not from any mountain bird they know. They've seen one like it twice on the trail recently, wheeling north.

skillChecks.context: Sense of being watched — passive or active.

tiers.outcome: Nothing.
A vague sense of being watched. No specifics.
The watching has a direction — north, ahead, somewhere past the next ridges. Whatever is watching is not close. But it knows you are here.
All the above. Plus: the watching is intermittent, not constant. As if something looks, then turns away, then looks again — patrolling rather than fixated.

All the above. Plus: the PC realizes the bat they saw twice was NOT the same bat. Different size, different wing-shape. There are at least two of them, possibly more, and they have been watching the party's progress for longer than two days.

skillChecks.context: Healer assesses altitude effects on the party.

tiers.outcome: Everyone seems tired but fine.
Slowed reactions, shorter wind. Optional rule: -1 to Athletics/Acrobatics for sustained physical effort at this elevation until they descend or acclimate.

All the above. Plus: Tyr is doing measurably worse than the others. He's pushing through, but his sleep is poor and his color is off. (Reflects the carried-over nightmare mechanic — DC 12 INT before each long rest.)

All the above. Plus: Adrik is acclimated to high elevations in a way the others aren't. Either he climbs frequently — or he's spent extended time in mountains recently. (Adrik was in the cove for unknown duration before S18.)

All the above. Plus: the healer notes that Borin's heart-rate spikes when he uses Rumor of the Earth — there is a physical cost to that ability the party hadn't noticed. Mention but don't mechanize unless Josh wants to develop it.

branches.condition: Party wants to hunt or pause
branches.outcome: → Scene 2 (the switchback / the hunting decision)

branches.condition: Party pushes through and skips hunting
branches.outcome: → Scene 2 still — bat ambush still finds them at the switchback, just with everyone present. No party split. Worse positioning for the bats.

scenes.title: The Hunting Detour
scenes.subtitle: Party splits at the switchback
scenes.trigger: End of Scene 1. Party at a switchback with daylight to spare. DM lets them choose: keep climbing or pause to hunt.
scenes.location: A switchback in the trail. From the upper loop, a steep gully drops 80 ft into rocky scrub where mountain goats have left fresh sign. The trail folds back on itself; lower loop visible from above.
scenes.lighting: Mid-to-late afternoon, ~3 PM. Sun still well up. Roughly 3–4 hours of full daylight remain. Wind blowing down the gully — favorable for a stalk.
scenes.readAloud:
The trail folds back on itself at a sharp switchback. From the higher loop, you can see the lower loop perhaps eighty feet below. Between them, a steep gully drops away — choked with scrub juniper and loose scree, the kind of slope a careful person could descend in fifteen minutes. There is sign in the gully: dropped pellets, a hoof-scuff on a stone, the mineral salt-smell of mountain goat. Someone, somewhere down there, ate well last week. The wind is at your back, blowing down the gully — favorable for a stalk.

Tyr leans against the rock at the switchback for a moment. Catches his breath. Doesn't say anything. The others notice. He waves them off.
scenes.purpose: 1) Justify a party split (small hunting group descends, others stay at switchback). 2) Plant Tyr's exhaustion atmospherically (the lean, the pause). 3) Set up the bat ambush in Scene 3. 4) Optional Nat 20 plants: orc footprint, distant tower silhouette.
dmNotes: PARTY SPLIT: Likely volunteers for hunt: Mungo, Dudo, Adrik, Gilgamesh (light/agile/scouts). Likely stays: Borin, Carl, Tyr. Don't force the split — let it emerge from RP. Push back gently if everyone wants the same side.
TYR'S EXHAUSTION: He CAN descend the gully if he tries. But describe him stopping halfway, breath ragged, hands on knees. He makes it. No mechanical penalty unless Gabe leans into it.

BAT-SPOTTING TIMING (CRITICAL): Bats can position freely overhead during active tracking — eyes are DOWN. NO Perception check during the hunt itself. Bats accumulate over an unsuspecting party. This is a feature, not a bug.

PERCEPTION CHECK ONLY HAPPENS AT TRANSITION POINTS: (1) If trail goes cold (Survival < 10) — hunters give up and look up. (2) When kill is made and they hike back — they look up to navigate the climb.

SWITCHBACK GROUP also has eyes DOWN — watching the hunters from above. They get a Perception check only when the hunters' transition point happens, since they look up too if they hear/see something change.
ALPHA TARGETING: When grapple attempted, target is RANDOM among Dudo / Mungo / Adrik (lightest PCs). Roll d3.
ABDUCTION DIFFICULTY: Alpha drops its prey only at 25% HP — that's 11 HP or less out of 44. Needs 33+ damage in 1-2 rounds to prevent. Highly likely to succeed unless party focus-fires aggressively.
OPTIONAL SETUP BEATS: Carl irritable joke about Tyr lounging (Tyr doesn't reply). Mungo naps on rock. Gilgamesh sketches. Borin checks the stone again — still YES, within 3 miles, no specifics.

skillChecks.context: Whoever leads the hunt — eyes are DOWN, no Perception possible during this roll.

tiers.outcome: Hunters lose the trail in the scree. Find nothing, waste 60–90 minutes. Light starting to slant when they regroup. TRAIL GOES COLD → Transition Point 1 → Perception check available.
Locate goat sign within 30 minutes. Within bow range of two goats. Roll attack normally (DEX or ranged, AC 11, HP 9 each). On kill, hike back → Transition Point 2 → Perception check available.
Same but faster — 20 minutes to find. Two goats within bow range. On kill, hike back → Transition Point 2 → Perception check available.

All the above. Plus: while tracking, the hunter notices something OFF in the soil — a half-buried impression, NOT a goat hoof. Heavy. Booted. Can't stop to examine without breaking the stalk; mark it for later. (Adrik or Borin can recognize 'boot, not goat' if asked — but don't volunteer this.)

All the above. Plus: the impression is unmistakably a ORC FOOTPRINT. Recent — within the last day or two. Heading uphill, not down. The hunter recognizes what it means: someone has been hunting this gully too, and they didn't come back the way they went.

skillChecks.context: Available ONLY at: (1) trail-cold give-up moment, OR (2) hike back from kill. Multiple PCs at the transition each roll separately — highest result determines outcome.

tiers.outcome: Nothing. The sky is just sky. Continue back to switchback or keep moving.
The wind has shifted. Animal sounds have stopped. Something is wrong, but the hunter can't say why. → Roll initiative when ambush hits. Scene 3B (Surprise Ambush).
Three or four large shapes wheeling against a high cloud, descending. The hunter has time to shout a warning, ready a weapon, take cover. → Scene 3A (Forewarned Ambush).

All the above. Plus: the hunter sees the iron harness on the largest one. This is not random predation — these bats are being commanded. Roll initiative with ONE round of preparation; the hunting group acts before the bats. → Scene 3A with surprise on the bats.

All the above. Plus: the hunter glimpses, on a far ridge perhaps three miles north, the unmistakable silhouette of a stone TOWER cut into the mountain face. It's there for a moment in the changing light, then the angle shifts and it's gone. They have seen something built. (DM: this is Amon Lhuin. Don't say the name.)

branches.condition: Anyone passes Perception ≥ 15 at a transition point
branches.outcome: → Scene 3A — Forewarned Ambush. Hunters and watchers have time to react.

branches.condition: Everyone fails Perception (< 15) at the transition point, or party never has a transition point
branches.outcome: → Scene 3B — Surprise Ambush. Bats descend before anyone realizes.

branches.condition: Party skips the hunt entirely, keeps climbing
branches.outcome: → Scene 3B but with everyone together. No party split. Bats still ambush — Alpha targets the lightest exposed PC.

scenes.title: Forewarned Ambush
scenes.subtitle: Bat combat — hunters warned
scenes.trigger: Anyone passes Perception ≥ 15 at a transition point in Scene 2.
scenes.location: The hunting gully (lower zone) and the switchback above. ~80 ft of vertical separation. Bats enter from above the gully.
scenes.lighting: Failing afternoon light. Sun dropping toward western ridge. Long shadows in gully. ~30–60 min until sunset. Wind steady from north (down the gully).
scenes.readAloud: The shout goes up first — someone has spotted them. The warning carries down the gully and up to the switchback in the same breath. Time slows to that strange clarity that comes before violence: weapons coming free, hands finding rock to crouch behind. Above you, four shapes drop out of the cloud cover like falling stones. A fifth is bigger. Wider. Something glints on its chest. They are coming fast.
scenes.purpose: Bat combat with the party split. Determine end-state (abduction successful / abduction prevented / bats killed). Forewarned setup: hunters have cover/weapons readied, warning relayed up to switchback group. Standard initiative for everyone.
dmNotes: BATTLEFIELD: 3 vertical zones. UPPER (switchback, +80 ft elevation, where remainers stayed). GULLY (combat floor, ~50×80 ft, scrub juniper, scree). AERIAL (60–200 ft above gully, where bats fly). Half-cover behind boulders. Difficult terrain on scree (half movement).
INITIATIVE: Standard 5e individual initiative. Suggested grouping: PCs individual, Couriers as group (single slot) or individual (per Jesse's preference), Alpha as separate slot.
ALPHA TACTICS: Round 1, enters at ~120 ft up. Closes distance. Round 2+, attempts grapple on closest qualifying target (Dudo/Mungo/Adrik — random d3 if multiple in reach).
COURIER TACTICS: Dive-attack from 60+ ft up. After attack, fly out of melee reach (60 ft fly speed). Goal is harass and break up rescue attempts. Retreat when 1 remaining.

GRAPPLE MECHANIC: Alpha makes Athletics +5 vs target's Athletics OR Acrobatics. If Alpha wins, target is grappled AND immediately flies upward at half speed (50 ft/round, AC drops to 11 burdened). If target wins, no grapple this turn.

ABDUCTION PREVENTION: Path 1 = damage Alpha to ≤11 HP (25% of 44, requires ~33 dmg). Path 2 = creative tactics (net, grapple bat, knock prone in flight, entangle, sever harness, jump on bat). Rule generously on creative options — see skill check tables.

SWITCHBACK GROUP: Three options each round. (1) Fire from range — shortbow disadvantage beyond 80 ft, longbow fine to 150 ft, wind imposes -2 to ranged attacks vs bats. (2) Climb down — Athletics/Acrobatics DC 12, fail = falling damage and 2-3 round delay. (3) ROPE (DISCOVERABLE) — if any PC says they're rigging rope, DC 10 to descend safely in 1 round. Reward initiative.
WEATHER: Wind from north imposes -2 to PC ranged attacks vs bats. Bats unaffected (they're banking with the wind).
RETREAT CONDITIONS: Couriers retreat at 1 remaining. Alpha drops grappled prey at ≤11 HP and retreats. If Alpha killed before grapple lands, couriers' morale breaks within 1 round.

skillChecks.context: If knocked prone or forced movement on scree.

tiers.outcome: Slip, prone, half movement next round.
Recover footing, half movement this round.
No effect — handle the scree fine.

skillChecks.context: Examines harness fragments and bodies after the fight.

tiers.outcome: Just dead bats.
The harness on the Alpha is military-grade leather and metalwork. Not from any beast-handler the party knows.
All the above. Plus: harness is fitted with Númenórean ironwork — Tyr or Adrik would recognize the smithing tradition.

All the above. Plus: ADRIK specifically recognizes dwarven rivetwork holding the harness together. The metal is OLD — older than Pharazôr's involvement. Made by reusing dwarven craft from somewhere nearby.
All the above. Plus: a small symbol stamped into the inner harness — a stylized bird-of-prey silhouette. (DM: this is Pharazôr's mark. Don't name it. Surface again later.)

skillChecks.context: If the party pursues after combat.

tiers.outcome: The bats came from the north. That's all you can say.
From a peak roughly 2-3 miles north. There is structure on that peak — maybe a tower silhouette in the failing light.
All the above. Plus: clear flight pattern showing the bats have been making this run repeatedly — same flight lanes, well-worn.
All the above. Plus: blood spots on the trail leading north (party blood on bat claws, dropped during retreat). The trail can be followed even at night with a torch.
All the above. Plus: tracker spots orc boot prints at the trail's start, mingled with the bat blood. Whatever ground patrols come from the same place the bats do.

branches.condition: A — Successful Abduction (Alpha escaped with prey)
branches.outcome: → Scene 4 (transition) → Scene 5A (captive POV) and Scene 5B (rescuers POV) IN PARALLEL.
→ Scene 4 (search corpses, find harness lineage) → Scene 5B (track north).

branches.condition: C — Failed Abduction (Alpha dropped prey, retreated)
branches.outcome: → Scene 4 (everyone alive but bruised) → Scene 5B.
DM call. Most likely retreat to cove or mass capture → Scene 5A with multiple captives.

scenes.title: Surprise Ambush
scenes.subtitle: Bat combat — hunters caught flat-footed
scenes.trigger: Everyone fails Perception (< 15) at the transition point, OR party never reached a transition point.
scenes.location: Same as 3A — gully and switchback, ~80 ft vertical.
scenes.lighting: Same as 3A — failing afternoon, long shadows, wind from north.
scenes.readAloud: The first you know is the sound — not a screech, not a roar, but the hard percussive WHUMP of leathern wings folding into a dive. Three feet from your face, something the size of a hunting dog has its claws out. Then another. Then another. And rising over them, blocking what's left of the sun, the shape of something WIDER, an iron flash on its chest as it banks for its angle. Roll initiative.
scenes.purpose: Bat combat — but with TRUE SURPRISE for the hunting group. Same battlefield and tactics as 3A, but the Alpha gets a free first action. Abduction is highly likely.
dmNotes: TRUE SURPRISE — round 1 rule: Hunting group PCs CANNOT act on round 1 (they are surprised per 5e rules). They cannot move, cannot take actions, cannot use reactions until start of round 2.

ALPHA FREE ACTION: Before initiative is rolled, the Alpha makes ONE free grapple attempt against a randomly chosen target. Roll d3: 1=Dudo, 2=Mungo, 3=Adrik (whichever are in the hunting group). Use the standard grapple mechanic — Alpha Athletics +5 vs target's Athletics OR Acrobatics. If Alpha wins, the target is grappled and lifted (Snatch and Carry).
COURIERS ACT NORMALLY ROUND 1: Couriers roll initiative and act on their turn with full actions. They dive on the hunting group while the Alpha begins its escape with the grappled PC.

SWITCHBACK GROUP NOT SURPRISED: They roll initiative normally and CAN act on round 1, but they're 80 ft above and reacting to confusion below — they may need a moment to figure out what's happening. They have full actions but limited tactical options on round 1.
ROUND 2 ONWARD: Standard initiative for everyone. Hunting group can finally act. Alpha is already at altitude with prey if grapple succeeded — pursuit is now the question.
ALL OTHER MECHANICS IDENTICAL TO 3A — see Scene 3A DM notes for: battlefield zones, courier tactics, switchback descent options, prevention paths, retreat conditions.
DANGER LEVEL: Meaningfully higher than 3A. Free grapple attempt + lost round of action means Alpha is likely flying off with a PC by round 2. Players will need to react FAST or commit to pursuit.

skillChecks.context: All skill check tables (Athletics, Investigation, Survival) work identically. See Scene 3A for full tables.

tiers.outcome: Reference Scene 3A's skill check tables — surprise mechanic only changes round 1 action economy, not check resolution.

branches.outcome: Reference Scene 3A — A (abduction), B (Alpha killed), C (prey dropped), D (TPK) all apply.

scenes.title: The Carry
scenes.subtitle: Transition — route to Scene 5
scenes.trigger: End of Scene 3A or 3B — bats are dead, fled, or have a captive. Combat is over.
scenes.location: The gully and switchback. Same battlefield, post-combat. Bat corpses where they fell. Possibly PC blood on the rocks.
scenes.lighting: Sunset arriving — perhaps 30–45 min of usable light remaining. Long shadows. Wind still steady from the north.
scenes.purpose: Transition scene. Confirm which end-state happened. Give the party a beat to process. Route to Scene 5A and/or 5B. NOT a content scene — it's a hinge. Don't pad it. Most mechanics already live in Scene 3A's skill check tables.
dmNotes: BRANCH A (Successful Abduction): Captive flown north. Read 'The shape of it doesn't quite register at first...' Pause; ask captive PC privately what their character notices/feels in that moment (NOT escape — that's Scene 5A). Then return to surviving party for the pursuit decision.
BRANCH A — Routing: Scene 5A (captive POV) and Scene 5B (rescuers POV) run IN PARALLEL going forward. DM cuts between them at natural beats.

BRANCH A — Pursuit decision: (1) Pursue NOW in failing light → Scene 5B begins immediately. (2) Camp and pursue at dawn → Scene 5B with prisoner clock advanced (1 pit prisoner risks dying overnight). (3) Split — DM call on logistics.

BRANCH B (Alpha killed before grappling): Read 'The Alpha hits the ground hard...' Couriers fled north. Use Scene 3A's Investigation table for harness inspection — whoever rolls highest gets the result. Do NOT pre-script which PC investigates.

BRANCH C (Alpha dropped prey): Read 'The grip breaks...' Roll 1d6 per 10 ft for falling damage on the dropped PC. Pause briefly — let the player describe how their character is reacting emotionally. Not a roll, just a beat.

CRITICAL — DO NOT name a specific Númenórean smithing-house here. Even on a Nat 20 Investigation, the party learns 'Númenórean style' but NOT 'made by THAT house in THAT era.' Pharazôr's lineage recognition is saved for Scene 8 — that's the big reveal moment.
All branches B and C route to Scene 5B (track north or camp).
BRANCH D (TPK / near-TPK): DM call. Most likely retreat to cove → end session early. If mass capture → Scene 5A with multiple captives, skip Scene 5B.

skillChecks.context: Investigation (harness search), Survival (track bats), Athletics (footing) — all five-tier tables live in Scene 3A. Scene 4 doesn't introduce new mechanics; it routes outcomes.

tiers.outcome: See Scene 3A — five-tier ladder with Nat 20 plant of Pharazôr's bird-of-prey symbol.
See Scene 3A — five-tier ladder for tracking the bats north.

branches.condition: A — Successful Abduction (Alpha escaped with prey)
branches.outcome: → Scene 5A (captive POV) and Scene 5B (rescuers POV) IN PARALLEL.
→ Scene 5B (track north or camp).

branches.condition: C — Alpha grappled but dropped prey when wounded
branches.outcome: → Scene 5B.
DM call: retreat to cove (end session) OR mass capture → Scene 5A with multiple captives.

scenes.title: The Pit
scenes.subtitle: Captive POV — only if abducted
scenes.trigger: A PC was abducted in Scene 3/4. Run in PARALLEL with Scene 5B (split-screen DMing).
scenes.location: Circular pit, ~30 ft across, ~20 ft deep, dwarven stonework. Below the lower workings of Amon Lhuin. Above: cracked vault of an old chamber, daylight bleeding through fractures. Around the captive: 9 swamp village survivors. MEZ is among them.
scenes.lighting: Twilight bleeding into night. Light from cracks above is grey and weakening.
scenes.readAloud:
You are dropped. Fifteen feet, maybe twenty. Stone underfoot — old stone, dwarf-cut, the corners worn smooth by centuries. You taste blood. Your weapon is somewhere — you don't know where. The light comes from cracks in the vault above, weak and grey, and there are people here. Nine of them, maybe more in the dark you can't see. Some are sitting against the walls. Some are lying down and not moving in a healthy way. One of them is watching you, and you know him.

It is Mez. The innkeeper. From the village in the swamp. He has lost weight. He looks like he hasn't slept in weeks. His face is the same and not the same. He sees you, and his expression doesn't change at all.
scenes.purpose: 1) Give the captive a moment that's THEIRS — quiet, claustrophobic, alone in the dark. 2) Land the 'you left us' beat through Mez (a known character). 3) Build the lair atmosphere — sounds from above, evidence of long use. 4) Set up the rescue arrival in Scene 7.
dmNotes: IF CAPTIVE IS ADRIK: His pendant is BURNING. The shard is well within ½ mile, in this lair. Pull Christian aside: 'The pendant is hotter than it has ever been. It's pulling toward the eastern wall of this pit — there's something behind that wall. Close. Maybe within fifty feet.' Christian decides what to share/risk.

MEZ CONTEXT: After the party killed Maldwin and walked away from the village in S17.2, the bat swarms came. Pharazôr's network harvested the survivors over weeks. The 9 prisoners are what's left of ~48 villagers. Mez survived because he was useful (cooking for prisoners). He's been here ~3 weeks.
MEZ'S 'YOU LEFT US' BEAT: He doesn't shout. He doesn't rage. He's been here too long for either. Use the dialogue seeds — paraphrase, don't read verbatim. Keep his voice flat, factual.

RHYTHM: Cut to/from Scene 5B at natural breaks. Good rhythm: 3-5 min with captive, then 'meanwhile, the rescue party...' for 5-7 min, then back. Don't let either thread go more than 10 min without a check-in.
WHEN RESCUERS ARRIVE (end of Scene 7): the two threads merge. Captive's actions in 5A may shape what rescuers walk into.
dialogueSeeds: You said the world was different now. After Maldwin. You said we were safe.
My wife was the price for fifteen winters of safety. You broke the pact. They came for the rest of us in three days.
I don't blame you for leaving. I blame you for thinking we would be alright.

skillChecks.context: The Alpha's grip flung the weapon somewhere; pit may have other things to find.

tiers.outcome: Can't find the weapon. Could be in the pit, the chamber above, or lost.
Locate the weapon nearby, within reach in the pit.
All the above. Plus: notice that Mez is hiding something small in his hand (a sharp piece of dwarven stone, used as a tool — he'll give it to the captive if asked).

All the above. Plus: notice that the wall on the east side of the pit has a hairline fracture running floor to ceiling — the stonework here has been DISTURBED, possibly within recent years. (DM: this is the alcove sealing for the shard.)

All the above. Plus: a tally scratched into the wall in dwarven runes — Adrik can read it (or relay to Adrik later). It marks 60+ prisoners across the years. This pit has held many cycles of captives.

skillChecks.context: Walls are slick old dwarven stone, ~20 ft.

tiers.outcome: Lose grip immediately. 1d6 falling damage. Back to the floor.
Get halfway, lose grip, fall. 1d6 falling damage. Back to the floor.
Climb to the rim. 8 hours of effort. Captive is exhausted (1 level).
Climb to the rim in ~10 minutes. No exhaustion. The chamber above is part of the lair — solo exploration. (DM: see Scene 7.)

All the above. Plus: as they reach the rim, they spot something — at the far end of the chamber above, a SMALLER second pit covered by a wooden grate. Sounds come from below it. (DM: where prisoners are processed individually — empty currently, but a chilling detail.)

skillChecks.context: What's happening in the lair from down in the pit.

tiers.outcome: Just the sounds of the pit — breathing, shifting, wind through cracks.
Boot-falls overhead, irregular. At least two people walking somewhere in the lair, occasionally crossing the upper chamber.
All the above. Plus: a third set of sounds — distant, from much higher up — sounds like the bats returning to roost.

All the above. Plus: a man's voice, far away, speaking in a measured cadence. Cannot make out words. Has the SHAPE of a long monologue or recitation. (DM: Pharazôr in his chambers — he reads aloud at this hour every evening.)

All the above. Plus: the captive recognizes that the recitation is in TWO LANGUAGES, alternating — Westron and one other. The other is uncomfortable to listen to even at this distance. (DM: Black Speech.)

branches.outcome: → Scene 7 (when rescuers arrive)
→ Scene 7 — solo lair exploration. Risk of capture by orcs or worse.

branches.condition: Captive talks to prisoners / searches pit
branches.outcome: → Information gained, atmosphere built. Rescue still required.

scenes.title: The Trail
scenes.subtitle: Rescuers POV — track the bats north
scenes.trigger: Bats have flown north (with or without a captive). Run in parallel with Scene 5A if there's a captive.
scenes.location: Trail above the switchback, ascending into thinner air toward the peak. Becomes more exposed and colder with elevation.
scenes.lighting: Sunset → dusk → first stars. Wind shifts unpredictably at higher altitude.
scenes.readAloud: The bats are gone before you can ready a second arrow. Whatever direction 'north' is from here, that is where they went — over the ridges, over a notch, into country you have not yet climbed. The wind shifts. The cold is harder now. Below you the gully goes dark first; above you, the ridge holds the last red of the sun. You have perhaps an hour before full dark.
scenes.purpose: 1) Get the party from gully to Amon Lhuin. 2) Activate Adrik's pendant at the right narrative moment. 3) Plant the dropped letter on Nat 20 (massive foreshadowing payload). 4) Build pre-lair atmosphere: cold, exposed, the silhouette growing closer.
dmNotes: PACING: Compress aggressively. Full journey from gully to Amon Lhuin is ~2-3 hours of in-world hiking. Run as one Survival check + 2-3 atmospheric beats + pendant activation + tower silhouette reveal. Don't roleplay every step.

ADRIK'S PENDANT — SPECIFIC TRIGGER: At the moment the party crests a ridge and FIRST sees the tower silhouette, the pendant goes warm in Adrik's hand simultaneously. Christian decides whether/how to react. Let him steer.
PRISONER CLOCK: If Survival < 15, forced camp = 6-8 hours lost = 1 of the 9 pit prisoners may not survive overnight. The party has to choose: push on without sleep, or pay the cost.

THE LETTER (Nat 20 only): Half-page parchment, broken black wax seal with bird-of-prey silhouette (matches harness mark from S3A). Mostly Westron, switches to Black Speech mid-letter. Tyr can attempt INT (Investigation) DC 14 to translate Black Speech (he glimpsed it in Eli/booklet thread).

LETTER PAYLOAD: Don't explain to players. Foreshadowing is what the letter IS. Key beats embedded: (1) shipments north — supply chain. (2) Maldwin's pact was one of many ('older arrangements in the swamps... one of the smaller pacts has gone quiet'). (3) Pharazôr has agents in Lake Town's council ('the new agreement at the lake-town progresses... draw the bait in') — DIRECTLY connects to Palantír mission. (4) Pharazôr is autonomous from his master ('He has not written in eight moons... what He does not know is the second matter') — Pharazôr is hiding the shard agenda from Gothmog. (5) 'Ph.' signature — players may connect to Pharazôr later.

ATMOSPHERIC BEATS (use 2-3): Wind dies suddenly then returns. Scrap of leather harness in scrub. Distant view of gully far below. Single bat call far north, nothing answers. Tyr's exhaustion shows (hands on knees, Carl helps wordlessly).
SESSION-END OPTION: If forced camp (Survival < 15) and table is running long, end session at camp as cliffhanger. Resume at dawn next session.

skillChecks.context: The bat trail leads north over ridges in fading light.

tiers.outcome: Lost in the dark. Forced camp. Lose 8 hours. Prisoner clock advances — 1 of 9 pit prisoners may not survive overnight.
Trail followed for ~1 mile. Lost in the dark. Forced camp. Lose 6 hours. Prisoner clock advances.
Trail followed all the way to a tower silhouette on a high ridge. Party reaches Amon Lhuin's outer slope before midnight. → Scene 6.
All the above. Plus: tracker spots that the orc boot prints from S18's cove track UP this same trail — they go up and don't come back down. Pharazôr's ground guards live here.

All the above. Plus: in scrub off the trail, the tracker finds A SEALED LETTER dropped by a courier bat. Black wax seal with bird-of-prey silhouette (matches harness from S3A). See dialogue seeds for letter content.

dialogueSeeds: [THE LETTER — read on Nat 20 Survival] Cousin — The work continues as agreed. The shipments north have not been disturbed and the older arrangements in the swamps hold for the moment, though I am told one of the smaller pacts has gone quiet. Look into it when you can spare the time. There is no urgency. The villagers there will not last another two winters at the current rate, and the matter resolves itself either way.
[LETTER continued] The new agreement at the lake-town progresses. Their council remains useful. I expect to draw the bait in within the season.

[LETTER — Black Speech section, alien script. Tyr INT DC 14 to translate.] He has not written in eight moons. The hand-that-holds knows what we built and approves it; what He does not know is the second matter. Keep it so. Burn this when read.
[LETTER signature, back to Westron] — yours in the long work, Ph.

branches.outcome: → Scene 6 — Approach to Amon Lhuin.
Lose hours, prisoner clock advances. Resume at dawn → Scene 6. (Optional session-end cliffhanger.)

scenes.title: Approach to Amon Lhuin
scenes.subtitle: First sight of the tower
scenes.trigger: End of Scene 5B. Party crests the final ridge. Adrik's pendant has activated.
scenes.location: High saddle between two peaks, ~quarter-mile from tower's outer slope. THREE-STACKED LAIR: Númenórean watchtower (carved into granite face), natural cave mouth (below tower's base), dwarf-cut doorway (deeper than the cave, OLDER work). The doorway seal has been broken — recently.
scenes.lighting: Full night. Waxing moon. Yellow candle/lamp light burning in tower's highest window. Wind moderate from the north.
scenes.readAloud:
The trail crests the final ridge, and you all stop walking at the same moment. None of you decided to. None of you needed to. The thing on the next peak is older than anything you have seen in the wilderness — older than the swamp village's lottery, older than the bears in the cove, older than the Last Alliance. It is older than story.

Three stories of cut grey stone, fitted into the mountainside as if the mountain had grown around it. The lines are too vertical, too proud, too sad to be dwarf-work. Half the upper crenellations are gone — broken off cleanly, by something that struck. One window — the highest one — burns with steady yellow light. Something is awake up there.

Below the tower's foundation, the mountain opens its own mouth: a cave, natural, going back into shadow. And deeper still, where the cave wall would have been solid, you can make out an arched doorway of cut stone. Older work than the tower above. Different hands. The seal has been broken — recently.

Adrik's pendant is wrapped in cloth now. Even through the cloth, the heat is undeniable. The signal is not pulling toward the tower. It is pulling DOWN — toward the cave, toward the deeper doorway, toward the stone the mountain has been keeping.
scenes.purpose: 1) Land the moment of arrival — let the party FEEL the age and weight. 2) Reveal the three-stacked-level lair geography. 3) Pendant escalation: now actively pointing toward lower workings. 4) Surface Tyr/Adrik lore beats through History rolls. 5) Let the party choose how to approach (no forced check).
dmNotes: PENDANT ESCALATION: 5B (½-mile threshold) = warm. Scene 6 (outer slope) = hot, wrapped. Scene 7 (lower workings) = burning, pulling visibly. Christian decides what Adrik shares.

NO FORCED STEALTH CHECK: Present the situation, let table choose approach. Possible choices: (1) Sneak (DC 14 group/rogue-leads), (2) Open approach, (3) Wait and observe (long rest, prisoner clock advances), (4) Split the party, (5) Direct confrontation (Pharazôr may speak from window).

WHAT'S HAPPENING IN THE LAIR RIGHT NOW: 3 orcs in tower's ground-floor guardroom (2 awake changing shifts, 1 asleep). Pharazôr in third-floor chambers reading aloud (per Scene 5A's Nat 20 plant). 2-3 bats in cave roost (wounded survivors from S3 combat, possibly Alpha if it survived). 9 prisoners in the lower workings pit. Shard sealed in alcove in side gallery of lower workings.

ADRIK'S DWARVEN HOLD NAME (placeholder): Karak Melúrz. Khuzdul-style construction (Karak = fortress prefix used in Tolkien for Khazad-dûm etc.; Melúrz invented). Christian can override or expand at any time — if he wants to develop it as Adrik's backstory, run with it.

TYR'S LORE BEAT (Nat 20): The broken crenellations suggest violence, not weather. Tyr feels in his bones this place was a LOSS, not a withdrawal. Don't say what happened — Pharazôr will name it later in Scene 8.
PERCEPTION ON THE LIT WINDOW: Higher rolls reveal the watcher's silhouette. Nat 20 reveals the recitation in two languages — Westron and Black Speech. Plants Pharazôr's identity through observation.
ANTICIPATE: If party chooses 'wait and observe' (option 3), prisoner clock advances. Be willing to fast-forward to morning — and remind party of the cost (1 prisoner may not survive).

skillChecks.context: Recognizing the watchtower's origin and history.

tiers.outcome: Old. Important once. Can't say more.
Númenórean construction. Second or Third Age work. Kind of watch-post Aragorn's people would have manned in better times.
Late Númenórean foothold-tower, kind built when kingdom was still expanding north and east. Almost certainly abandoned during Last Alliance era or shortly after. Three thousand years, give or take.
All the above. Plus: old shield-marks on the doorway. Faded. The crest of a noble house Tyr can almost — almost — name. (DM: leave ambiguous; Pharazôr will name it in Scene 8.)

All the above. Plus: Tyr knows in his bones this place was abandoned because something HAPPENED here. Not a withdrawal. A loss. The shape of the broken crenellations on the upper level suggests violence, not weather.

skillChecks.context: Recognizing the dwarven workings beneath.

tiers.outcome: Dwarven work, behind the cave. Old. Not anyone he knows.
An outpost. Small. Pre-Erebor era. Most likely a mining hold for a deposit that ran out.
The work is old enough that the carving conventions predate the styles Adrik was raised seeing — meaning the dwarves who built this were very old indeed. First or early Second Age dwarves, possibly.

All the above. Plus: there is a name carved into the doorway lintel. Adrik can read it: KARAK MELÚRZ. He doesn't know what it means or who founded it — the name is older than any dwarven holdings he was raised hearing about. (PLACEHOLDER — Christian can override or expand any time.)

All the above. Plus: Adrik knows this hold was NOT abandoned voluntarily. The carvings show signs of being defaced after the dwarves left — by hands that were not dwarves. The name was carved over an older, earlier inscription that has been chiseled out — what was written first is unrecoverable.

skillChecks.context: Anyone observing the tower from the saddle.

tiers.outcome: A single yellow light burning in the highest window. Steady. Doesn't flicker.
The light source is a candle or oil lamp, not a fire. Whoever's up there has been in that room for a while.
All the above. Plus: occasionally, a shadow moves across the window. Tall, slow-moving, deliberate. Not pacing — just shifting position.

All the above. Plus: the shadow's gait is not orcish. Whoever this is, they are not the kind of creature the party fought in the swamps. They are man-shaped, but their movement is UNUSUALLY SLOW — the pace of someone who has had centuries to learn that hurry doesn't matter.

All the above. Plus: faintly, on the wind, the watcher can hear a man's voice — alternating between Westron and another language. The one they don't recognize is uncomfortable to listen to. (DM: Black Speech. Pharazôr reading aloud from his desk.)

branches.outcome: → Scene 7, Level 1 (tower exterior approach, position to enter).
→ Scene 7, but orcs are alerted; combat possible at ground floor.

branches.condition: Wait and observe (long rest at saddle)
branches.outcome: Prisoner clock advances. → Scene 7 in morning, but prisoners may be reduced.
→ DM call on logistics. Scenes 7 and 5A (if captive) may overlap heavily.
→ Scene 8 may begin earlier. Pharazôr may speak from the tower window.

scenes.title: The Three Levels
scenes.subtitle: Lair exploration
scenes.trigger: The party enters the tower OR the cave OR the workings.
scenes.location: Amon Lhuin and below, in three vertically stacked sections.
scenes.runtime: 45–75 minutes real-time depending on what they explore.
scenes.purpose: Three thematic floors with different feels. Tyr's floor (watchtower), neutral middle (cave), Adrik's floor (workings).
dmNotes: LEVEL 1 — WATCHTOWER (Pharazôr's domain): Three stories. Ground floor: wrecked guardroom with the orc lair guards (NPC #3). Second floor: long-empty barracks; broken arrow-slits face the saddle. Third floor: Pharazôr's chambers — books in three languages including Adûnaic, a cold hearth, a chair that faces the north window, a desk with sealed correspondence. The lit window the party saw from outside is here. Orc combat possible if guards aren't bypassed (Stealth DC 14 to slip past). Pharazôr is on the third floor — if reached, GO TO SCENE 8. Letters on the desk (Investigation DC 12): up to three sealed letters, addressed in Westron to 'Brother Mehlin,' 'the Western Pact-Keeper,' and one untitled. Each implies a different Pharazôr-style operation elsewhere. NO Gothmog name in any of them.

LEVEL 2 — CAVE (the bat roost): A natural cavern beneath the tower's foundation. Bats live here when not on patrol — currently 2–3 sleeping on rock outcrops, plus the wounded survivors from Scene 3 if the party didn't kill them all. Between the cave and the tower above: a narrow vertical shaft with iron rungs, descending. Between the cave and the dwarven workings below: a passage, partly natural, partly widened by old picks. Stealth (DC 15) to move through without waking bats. The shaft to the tower is Pharazôr's 'front door' for couriers.

LEVEL 3 — DWARVEN WORKINGS (the shard): Down a stone passage, opening into what was once a small mining hold. Pillared chambers. A dry well in the center of one. Side galleries where the dwarves cut at the rock. The pit (Scene 5A) is at the far end of one of the larger chambers — cut originally as a refuse shaft, repurposed by Pharazôr. THE SHARD: at the end of one of the side galleries, sealed behind a wedged stone in a small alcove. Adrik's pendant points unmistakably here. The wedge is old. Investigating (DC 12) reveals that someone wedged it INTENTIONALLY — recently — sealing this alcove off, using a heavy stone and a hammered iron pin. Pharazôr did this. He believed it secure.
REMOVING THE WEDGE: Strength check DC 17, OR tools/time/leverage to extract it without breaking the alcove (10 minutes, no roll).

INSIDE THE ALCOVE: A pale fragment of crystal-like substance, about the size of a thumb. Not glowing in any visible way. Cold to the touch except where Adrik's pendant is — there, where the two come close, both objects warm to body temperature and resonate. Christian and Adrik will feel it.

SHARD MECHANICS: Undefined. Christian decides what shards do. For Session 19: small, portable, palpably significant, mechanically inert. Adrik can pocket it. He will know when more shards are near. If asked what it does NOW: nothing visible. If Christian asks for an Arcana check, let him roll — and if he hits 20+, give him a single sentence of his choice, not yours: 'You know one true thing about this object — what is it?' Christian writes the lore.

skillChecks.context: Slip past the orcs on the ground floor.

tiers.outcome: Bypass guards without combat.

skillChecks.context: Move through the bat roost without waking sleeping bats.

tiers.outcome: Pass without combat.

skillChecks.context: Read sealed letters on his desk.

tiers.outcome: Three sealed letters: 'Brother Mehlin,' 'the Western Pact-Keeper,' and one untitled. Implies wider operations. NO Gothmog name.

skillChecks.context: Brute-force the wedged stone sealing the alcove.

tiers.outcome: Wedge dislodges. Shard accessible.
Tools + 10 minutes, no roll.

skillChecks.context: Examining the pit interior — 5-tier table.

tiers.outcome: The pit is grim. There are people in it.
9 people. Swamp villagers. They have been here for weeks.
All the above. Plus: there are MORE sets of marks on the wall than 9 — older marks. Scratches. Many people have been kept here over the years. The pit is a long-running operation.
All the above. Plus: one set of marks shows a tally. Going by the tally, this pit has held perhaps 60+ people across the years.

All the above. Plus: among the older bones at the very bottom of the pit (largely buried), there is one that is not human. Investigation reveals it as an elf-bone — very old, very long-dead. The party doesn't have time or context to learn more.

branches.condition: Party reaches third floor of watchtower
branches.outcome: → Scene 8: Audience with Pharazôr
→ Scene 8 (DM judgment based on noise, time, stealth)

scenes.title: Audience with Pharazôr
scenes.subtitle: The session's emotional climax
scenes.trigger: Party reaches the third floor of the watchtower OR Pharazôr descends to confront them in the workings (DM judgment based on noise, time, and whether the party has been stealthy).
scenes.location: Pharazôr's chamber, third floor of the watchtower. OR wherever in the lair Pharazôr finds them. Pharazôr does NOT pursue if the party flees the area entirely.
scenes.lighting: Whatever the scene calls for. If in his chamber, lit by a single candle and the moon through the north window.
scenes.runtime: 25–40 minutes real-time depending on whether it ends in combat or a deal.
scenes.purpose: The Tyr-mirror beat. The shard reveal. The cliffhanger. The session's emotional core.
dmNotes: PHARAZÔR'S CHARACTER: Formal, patient, dangerous. Lived perhaps 800 years through means he does not explain. Speaks with the cadence of someone who has had too long to choose his words. NOT cartoonishly evil — sees himself as a steward of pacts that benefit both sides, a man who has made hard choices for a long arc of time. He believes Maldwin was a useful but limited tool. He believes the swamp villagers were a fair price for what their land yielded. He believes the prisoners in his pit are RESOURCES. He will say all of this without apology and without embarrassment if the conversation turns to morality. He is wrong, but he is sincerely wrong.
HE WILL OFFER TERMS BEFORE FIGHTING. Specifically:

→ If party HAS NOT yet recovered the shard: Safe passage out, in exchange for leaving the shard alone and not returning. 'There is something here that does not concern you. Walk away from it, and I will not impede you further.'

→ If party HAS recovered the shard: He offers to TRADE — he wants the shard, he will give them the prisoners' freedom in exchange. (His real plan: send the bats after them on their way out and recover both. But the offer is honest in the moment. He breaks it only if they refuse.)

→ If TYR is visible and armed: Before any of the above, Pharazôr names the Iron of Death — recognizes the smithing-house lineage — and offers Tyr alone an audience apart from the others. (DM: this is a Tyr-mirror moment. Don't script Tyr's response. Let Gabe play it.)

PARTIAL-AWARE OF ADRIK: At some point in the scene, Pharazôr looks directly at Adrik and says something like: 'You carry something that should not have come this far north. I cannot place it. But I feel it.' Christian decides what Adrik does with this.
dialogueSeeds: I have been here longer than your grandfather's grandfather drew breath.
Every agreement I have made was honored on my side.
Maldwin was a useful man. He was also a small man. He did not understand what he served.
The villagers in my pit are a renewable resource. Most of them came to me willingly, in the end.
You assume I am evil. Three thousand years ago, I would have agreed with you. You will not be alive in three thousand years to revise the question.
That sword. Lower it, please — not from fear. Because I knew the smith who made it. He was a good man. I would prefer not to see his work used poorly tonight.
What is it that you carry, dwarf? I cannot name it. But it sings to me, very faintly, and it should not be here.

skillChecks.context: 5-tier table.

tiers.outcome: He seems reasonable.
He is calm in a way that means he is not afraid of you. Take that as you will.
He is offering terms but he intends to break them. He is buying time. He has called for help (the bats are returning).
All the above. Plus: he is genuinely uncertain about Adrik. Whatever Adrik has, Pharazôr does NOT know what it is — and that uncertainty unsettles him. He is more dangerous because of it.

All the above. Plus: the party reads that Pharazôr is NOT acting alone. He answered to someone. He has not heard from that someone in some time, and that absence weighs on him. (Closest the party gets to a Gothmog hint this session. Still no name.)

branches.outcome: Pharazôr's bats arrive, OR the party draws first, OR Tyr can't bear what he hears and attacks. END the session ON the initiative roll. 'We'll start there next time.' (Recommended if energy is high.)

branches.condition: Cliffhanger B — Pharazôr's deal is on the table
branches.outcome: Players are debating it. Cut the session on the choice. 'Take a week to decide. We'll start there.' (Recommended if energy is medium.)

branches.condition: Cliffhanger C — Adrik claims the shard, Pharazôr reacts
branches.outcome: Pharazôr's sense of the pendant resolves — he understands what Adrik has just done. His face changes. End scene as he stands. 'He is no longer being patient.' (Recommended if Adrik's arc was the strongest thread of the night.)

wrapChecklist.label: Pharazôr seen or named on screen (or strong direct evidence: voice, journal, throne room)?
Adrik's pendant reacted visibly enough that the rest of the party noticed at least once?
Kill log: who landed final blow on each bat / each orc?
Notable rolls: every Nat 20 and Nat 1
New items: shard (if recovered), letters, harness ironwork, anything from Pharazôr's chamber
Tyr's exhaustion level at end of session
Tyr's nightmare save (DC 12 INT before the next long rest)
Adrik's pendant status — does he still have it? Did it cool down after the shard? Was it taken from him?
Foreshadowing dropped — which of the items above came up?
Ben's arc thematically referenced? (Pit prisoners' 'you left us' beat.)
Party's location at session end (in the tower? fled? camped on the slope?)
Prisoner status (alive and following the party? still in the pit?)
What's in the cliffhanger image — specific moment, specific tableau
